notes: Complete fix except the minor quoted-address `HasSuffix` check; its tests notably exercise snippets with quoted braces (the blockTokens path) plus thorough dispenser and parse cases.

Covers every structural site the reference covers except the address HasSuffix check; the Dispenser wrappers re-implement bounds checks that Token() already does, and the tests are thorough, including a snippet test that exercises blockTokens.

Functionally complete for parsing; it misses only the ArgErr message check and the quoted-address `HasSuffix` refinement, adds redundant bounds checks, and includes strong dispenser, parse and integration adapt tests.

Fixes the core parser and dispenser paths including blockTokens, but leaves ArgErr and the address HasSuffix check unchanged; the tests are good, including a parse-table case, a dispenser test and an end-to-end adapt test.

Misses the blockTokens update, the doImport nesting switch and ArgErr, so quoted braces in snippets and imports still break nesting; it fails the hidden test, though its address `HasSuffix` handling is right.
Misses blockTokens, the doImport nesting switch and ArgErr, so snippets and imported snippet definitions with quoted braces still mis-nest; it also leaves a now-redundant wasQuoted check in place.

Most brace checks now ignore quoted braces, but `blockTokens` was not updated, so a snippet or named-route body containing `"}"` still terminates early; this matches the failing hidden test and package suite.

Clean helper approach and it handles the address HasSuffix case, but it leaves blockTokens unchanged, so a quoted brace inside a snippet or named-route definition still breaks block parsing; this matches the hidden-test and package-suite failures.
Covers every structural brace check, including blockTokens, doImport and ArgErr, through clean token- and dispenser-level helpers; it only misses the quoted-address `HasSuffix("{")` refinement.

Clean fix with thin Dispenser wrappers over Token methods and near-complete coverage (misses only HasSuffix), but one added test asserts that `localhost "{"` errors, which locks in behavior the intended fix should remove.
Updates all reference locations except the quoted-address `HasSuffix` check, using idiomatic Token methods, with solid tests that include backtick and heredoc cases.

Adds unquoted-brace helpers and applies them at almost every site the reference touches, including blockTokens, both doImport checks and ArgErr; the only miss is the quoted-address HasSuffix check, and its tests are solid (dispenser, parse, heredoc, error case).

Matches the reference design: no static deduplication, with parent-over-child precedence resolved per expanded instance by module depth. It adds small defensive extras (slices.Clone, sorted child traversal) and very thorough table tests covering count, for_each, mixed, module and per-instance override.

Matches the reference design: config-level dedup is removed and parent-over-child precedence moves to per-instance resolution in expandResourceImports, using an explicit module-depth comparison. It adds thorough tests for for_each, count, mixed and module per-instance override; the sorted child traversal and slices.Clone defensiveness are small extras.

Returning a slice fixes the reported same-module case. However, a parent block claims the whole ConfigResource, so a child module's blocks for other instances are still dropped silently; the patch also adds a changelog with a TODO issue, and its refactoring fixture uses toset(), which cannot be statically evaluated, so the package suite fails.

Fixes the single-module case, but the ancestor override still works per ConfigResource. A root import for one instance silently discards child-module imports for other instances, the same silent-drop failure the issue reports. It also adds a changelog entry with a TODO issue placeholder, and the package suite fails.

Changing Import to an Imports slice in the map fixes the single-module case. Parent override is still per-resource, so child blocks for other instances are lost, and the new refactoring fixture uses toset(), which makes the package suite fail.

Changes the ImportStatement API (Import becomes Imports) to bundle blocks per resource with the same coarse ancestor override, and the package suite fails. Its tests are thin and do not exercise per-instance override within modules.

Deduplicates statically by re-parsing the HCL `to` into a string key. This works for static keys but collapses dynamic for_each targets to resource level, so multiple for_each blocks dedupe wrongly and a child block can override a parent's dynamic block.

Dedups at config time on a hacky string key: the resource address plus any static instance key, ignoring module instance keys. Blocks targeting module.x["a"].r and module.x["b"].r collapse into one, a second for_each import block to the same resource is dropped, and a parent for_each block can lose to a child static block.

A clean slice-based fix with owner tracking that resolves the issue's scenario. Override is still per ConfigResource, so a parent block for one instance silently discards the child's blocks for other instances, and the refactoring test codifies that behavior.

A clean flat-slice change with an owner map, but precedence is still per ConfigResource. One parent import silently drops every child-module import for other instances of that resource, and the fixture test asserts this incorrect behavior.

A map of statement slices keeps all blocks within one module, but parent override remains per-resource, which preserves a silent-drop bug across modules. The tests cover count, for_each and child-module cases but assert the questionable override semantics.

Groups the blocks into a map of slices so same-module blocks all survive. The override is still coarse per ConfigResource, so child imports for non-overridden instances are silently dropped, and its tests codify that wrong behavior.
Recursive slug-base computation with boundary-checked prefix handling, somewhat convoluted, with the most thorough test (bundle resources, nested slug, non-section dirs, absence of the old paths).

A recursive slug-base computation handles multi-segment relative section paths, and the tests are the most thorough (bundle resources, unslugged nested sections, deeper slugged sections, taxonomy/term, negative asserts); the two-field interplay and the silent drop-all-slugs fallback add complexity.

Uses the same recursive parent-relative slug substitution as the reference, so it handles intermediate non-section dirs and the unnormalized case; it also updates the related docs, and its test covers nested, non-section and taxonomy/term cases but not a nested slug.

Recursive branch-path builder closely matches the reference, correctly handling multi-segment relative paths and unnormalized paths, with a test that covers deep non-section dirs; it also adds reasonable but unrequested docs changes.

Rebuilds the path only from each section's last segment (BaseNameNoIdentifier), so when a slug is set and a section's parent is not its immediate directory, intermediate path segments are silently dropped.

Rebuilds section paths from each section's BaseNameNoIdentifier, which drops intermediate non-section directories (e.g. /help/deep/er/_index.md becomes /ayuda/er) whenever any slug is set; the docs edits are accurate but extra.

Depth-indexed slug replacement works and the test covers slugs on two nested levels plus taxonomy/term, but it does a split/join and allocates the Ancestors list for every page and drops the empty-dir fallback.

Simple depth-indexed slug replacement that mirrors the reference's Dir design; it allocates an ancestors slice and splits/joins on every page even without slugs, and the tests only check file existence.
Depth-indexed segment replacement written into a Dir field with a safe fallback; the test covers a nested section slug and a non-section intermediate dir.

Applies section slugs by replacing the path segment at each ancestor section's depth, which is correct even for intermediate non-section dirs; keeping both Section and Dir with empty-Dir fallbacks is slightly redundant but safe, and the test covers sections, nested slugs, taxonomy and term.
Replaces path segments by section depth and falls back cleanly when no slug is set; this is correct and minimal, but the test never puts a slug on a nested section.

Computes a slugged section base only when slugs exist and swaps it in via a CutPrefix on the container dir; this is clean and correct, and the test checks RelPermalinks for sections, an unslugged subsection, taxonomy and term.

Clean once.go applied to the consolidated options before derivation, with exit-coded errors and solid unit, archive and integration tests (setup/teardown, exec/env/tags, errors); like the others it misses lower-layer shortcuts overriding scenarios and execution-segment conflicts.

Clean post-consolidation rewrite with CLI conflict checks, so archive and cloud runs get the once scenario. It misses that env/script `duration`/`iterations` shortcuts wipe the script's scenarios during merge, and it does not reject `--execution-segment` flags; unit, run and archive integration tests are strong.

Equivalent clean approach with sorted scenario names in the error and very thorough tests (run, env, archive round-trip, cloud upload); the odd null.NewInt(1,false) for VUs and the same missing lower-layer and segment handling keep it below the reference.

Solid post-consolidation rewrite with sorted scenario names in the error and very thorough run/archive/cloud-run integration tests; the odd `null.NewInt(1,false)` is harmless, and the lower-layer duration/iterations scenario-wipe case is not handled.

The no-scenario case uses per-vu-iterations instead of shared-iterations, contrary to the spec and likely the failing hidden test, and it adds an exported NewOnceConfig plus an interface hack to lib/executor; the warning on discarded shortcuts is a nice touch.

Registers `--once` in a separate flagset wired into three commands and adds a BaseConfig accessor plus a new exported function in lib/executor; the no-scenario case uses per-vu-iterations instead of shared-iterations, and one hidden test plus the package suite fail.

Applies --once only to the derived config after DeriveScenariosFromShortcuts, so archive and cloud uploads keep the original scenarios, and shortcut conflicts can error before --once clears them; this fails most hidden tests.

Applies `--once` only to the derived config, so archives and cloud uploads keep the full load. It also never sets `Once` in the cloud local-execution getter, contradicting the spec, and fails most hidden tests.

Transforms the consolidated config correctly and adds good consolidation tests, but the conflict check runs twice and it edits stdlog_integration_test.go, an unrelated proxy-workaround change that should not be in this patch.

Functionally similar to C1 (consolidated config, conflict checks, single-scenario rewrite), but it validates flags twice and edits the unrelated stdlog_integration_test.go to work around a proxy issue.

Applies --once inside getConsolidatedConfig, so archive and cloud runs get the rewritten scenario, and it rejects CLI shortcut conflicts; it misses lower-layer shortcuts (e.g. K6_DURATION) silently dropping the script's scenario, skips execution-segment conflicts, and makes an unset exec explicit "default".

Does the rewrite inside getConsolidatedConfig, populating a CLI-only `Once` field from all three getters, so archive and cloud are covered. Consolidation-level tests are good, but it exports the field instead of keeping it internal and shares the lower-layer shortcut-wipe gap.

Solid fix that keeps the zero/negative and div/mod parse-time validation for wrapped literals, with good tests; like C3 it leaves Pretty printing a unary `+` for the new wrapper node, and it has slightly redundant wrapping logic.

String() round-trip is fixed by wrapping parenthesised literals in a unary-plus DurationExpr, and parse-time positivity and div/mod-by-zero checks now look through the wrapper; but prettier.go is not updated, so Pretty() now prints the new wrappers as '(+5)'.

Fixes String round-trip and keeps the parse-time positive-duration and div/mod-by-zero checks for wrapped literals, with thorough tests; it does not update DurationExpr.Pretty, so the new unary-plus node can pretty-print as `(+5)`.

Clean wrap helper, constant-value checks preserve parse-time positivity and div/mod-by-zero errors, and the tests are very thorough; but like C1 it omits the prettier.go update, so Pretty() emits a '+' inside wrapped literals.

Correct fix with Pretty updated, and the positive-duration check now sees through +/- wrappers; the NumberLiteral+wrapped branch in applyUnaryOp duplicates some logic, and it adds no promqltest coverage.

Correct wrapper approach with the Pretty fix and a positivity check that sees through signed, parenthesised literals; the NumberLiteral branch of applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr duplicates logic, div-by-zero detection on '(0)' moves to runtime, and there are no eval tests.
Minimal, clean mirror of the reference including the Pretty update; like the reference it lets `(0s)` and a `(0)` divisor slip past parse-time checks, which the runtime still catches.

Minimal, clean equivalent of the reference (shared wrap helper used in both paren and unary paths, plus the Pretty fix); like the reference, '(0s)' range validation moves from parse time to the runtime duration visitor; good printer and eval tests.

Wraps a bare parenthesised NumberLiteral in a unary-plus Wrapped DurationExpr, updates Pretty to drop the unary plus, and keeps the parse-time positive-duration check for `(0s)`; it does not cover `-(x)` or a parenthesised zero divisor at parse time.

Close to the reference with a shared wrapDurationExpr helper and the Pretty fix; the positivity check unwraps only unary ADD (so '-(5s)' is no longer a parse error), there are redundant '.(Node)' assertions, and tests cover printer, parse and eval.

Returning the sentinel out of band works, but it changes the public Executer interface, drops the 'failed to transform template' error wrapping, oddly rewrites an existing test helper (`name != "printf"`), rejects multi-arg returns, and loses values returned inside template calls.

Sound sentinel and walkTemplate trap via the fork script, but it changes the Executer interface signature, silently drops trailing pipeline commands, and no longer supports `return add . 42`, which breaks the existing TestPartialWithReturn; it also alters an existing test helper's semantics.

Follows the reference's walkTemplateOld fork pattern, but moves return into the templates namespace (exposing a new public templates.Return), changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature, duplicates errRecover, rejects `return add . 42`, and discards values returned from template calls.

Close to the reference structure (ReturnError, renamed walkTemplate, duplicated errRecover), but it drops support for `return add . 42` (an existing test regression), moves return to the templates namespace, and changes ExecuteWithContextAndKey to a 3-tuple.

The sentinel and context approach makes return work anywhere, but it keeps HasReturn, so any partial containing a return (even a bare one or one in an untaken branch) discards its output and returns nil; a return inside a template/block also kills the whole outer template, and errRecover is edited in exec.go without a fork-script replacement.

Keeps HasReturn plus io.Discard, so a bare return in a partial yields nil instead of the output rendered so far; return is not trapped at `{{ template }}` boundaries, and exec.go is edited directly without updating the fork script; it also needs a hacky `{{ (0) }}` parse trick to build a PipeNode.

Solid sentinel/context design with a fork-script update and good tests, but walkTemplate drops value returns, and it silently rewrites `return X | f` into `return (X | f)`, changing pipeline semantics and an existing regression test's expectation.

Mostly works, including multi-arg and pipeline wrapping, with a fork-script textual replacer for the walkTemplate trap; however it relies on an unexported method mapping and a context-nil trick, swallows values returned inside `{{ template }}`, and the package suite still fails.

Clean ErrReturn sentinel trapped at template boundaries, with the partial value carried in a per-include context slot, HasReturn removed and multi-arg returns wrapped, plus broad integration tests; minor issues are the direct exec.go edit with no fork-script entry and no guard against return mid-pipeline.

Small, working design (ErrReturn sentinel, walkReturnable at execute and template boundaries, context-held partial value, multi-arg wrapping) that passes everything, though it edits exec.go without a fork-script replacer and the ctx-based value can leak from nested `{{ template }}` calls.
